# Values

How each kind of value a field takes is written in JSON (04 §7.1). The page of each definition type says which kind each of its fields takes.

<a id="quantities"></a>
## Quantities

A number in the field's SI unit, or a string of a number and a unit: `"250 ms"`, `"70 kPa"`, `"-5 C"`. A rate is a quantity per time: `"0.012 kg/s"`, `"0.15 /h"`. The [units](units.md) page lists them. A time is kept in whole microseconds.

<a id="references"></a>
## References

A reference to a definition of type `T` (04 §7.1).

In data it is an id: a bare name, looked up in the namespace of the mod that wrote it and then in that mod's imports, or a qualified `namespace:name` (04 §4.3). It is resolved the moment it is read: a `Ref` always holds the dense id of a definition that exists. A dangling reference is a diagnostic at the exact position of the string, with the closest existing ids as suggestions.

A `Ref` can be the key of a map: `BTreeMap<Ref<DamageType>, Resist>` reads `{ "impact": { ... }, "blast": { ... } }`.

<a id="inline-definitions"></a>
## Inline definitions

A definition of type `T` given by id or written in place (04 §5).

Where a definition is expected inside another (a rule inside an action, a map piece inside a tract) it may be written inline in place of an id. The inline definition is loaded as a definition of its own and registered like any other; this field holds its dense id. Its id is `<parent id>#<path>`, which cannot be written as a reference, so it cannot be referred to from elsewhere. Given an `id` of its own, it is defined under that id in the mod's namespace and can be.

<a id="tags"></a>
## Tags

A free-form string given to definitions and tested by rules, interned to a number (04 §7.1).

The number is a position in the `TagTable` of the `Defs` it was loaded into: tags are numbered in sorted order, so the same mods always give the same numbers. A tag from one `Defs` means nothing in another; a save names tags by their strings.

<a id="texts"></a>
## Texts

Player-facing text (04 §7.1).

All player-facing strings use `Text`, so that a translation layer can be added later without touching definitions. A text may contain `{expression}` templates (05 §4.6).

A text holds the string as written, where it was written and, once its definition has compiled it, the compiled template. A definition type compiles its texts in `Def::compile`, saying what is in scope there:

and renders one with `Text::render`. A text that was never compiled renders as it was written.

<a id="expressions"></a>
## Expressions

An expression field (04 §7.1; 05 §7.1): a value worked out when it is asked for, of the type `T` says.

| Written | Meaning | |---------|---------| | `12`, `true`, `[1, 2]` | A literal | | `"self.var.kills * 2"` | An expression, when `T` is not a text or an id | | `"glass"` | The text or the id itself, when `T` is `Str` or `IdOf` | | `"250 ms"`, `"5 m/s"` | A quantity in SI units, when `T` is a number | | `{ "expr": "…" }` | An expression, always | | `{ "call": "fn", "args": { … } }`, `{ "count": query }`, … | A [value source](ValueSource) |

`T` is one of `Number`, `Int`, `Bool`, `Str`, `Any` and `IdOf<D>`. The field holds what was written and where; the definition type that owns it compiles it in `Def::compile`, saying what is in scope there, and after that `Expr::eval` gives its typed value.

<a id="conditions"></a>
## Conditions

A condition (05 §7.2): an expression that gives a boolean, or a structure of them.

| Written | Meaning | |---------|---------| | `"self.var.rage > 50"` | An expression | | `true`, `false` | A constant | | `{ "all": [ … ] }`, `{ "any": [ … ] }`, `{ "not": … }` | A structure; the three nest freely | | `{ "expr": "…" }` | An expression | | `{ "exists": query }` | Whether a query has any result (not built yet: it counts as false) |

A condition that comes to null counts as false (05 §4.4). `Cond::default()` always holds, which is what a rule with no `if` means.

<a id="parameters"></a>
## Parameters

A parameter's value: a type, or an object with the type in it.

<a id="queries"></a>
## Queries

A query selects a set of things: an object with one key, its kind, whose value holds the kind's arguments and `where`, `sort` and `limit` (05 §11). The [queries](queries.md) page lists the kinds.

<a id="effects"></a>
## Lists of effects

A list of effects (05 §10): a field type for any definition struct.

The field holds the list as it was written, with the place of every value, and, once its definition has compiled it, the tree the interpreter walks. A definition type uses it in three steps:

and runs it with `RuleSet::run_effects`, giving the values of the subjects and the locals in the order the scope bound them. A list that is not handed over is never compiled and does nothing when it is run.

Compiled this way a list is outside any rule: `return` in it is a load error. A rule compiles its own lists itself.

The [effects](effects.md) of the rule system and the [verbs](verbs.md) are what a list holds.

<a id="experimental"></a>
## Experimental fields

A field that is an experimental feature (04 §8.4).

Write the field as `Option<Gated<MyFeature, T>>` with `#[serde(default)]`. A definition that gives the field uses the feature: that is a load error unless the mod that wrote the value names the feature in its `mod.json`.

<a id="json"></a>
## Plain JSON

Any JSON value, read as it is. The world's area kinds and fields keep some of their settings this way until the world reads them.
